potato__early_blight.symptoms: Circular to angular dark brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings producing a target-board pattern, surrounded by chlorotic yellow halo on older lower leaves.
potato__early_blight.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Fungal pathogen producing dark, beaked, muriform conidia produced on short conidiophores. Survives in crop debris and infected seed tubers.
potato__early_blight.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) alternating with wet and dry periods; relative humidity >80%; frequent dew or overhead sprinkler irrigation.
potato__early_blight.transmission_mechanism: Air-borne conidia, wind dispersal, rain splashing from soil debris to lower foliage.
potato__early_blight.diagnostic_characteristics: Distinct circular to angular dark brown-black target-board spots with concentric rings surrounded by a chlorotic yellow halo.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Lacks prominent concentric target rings and stays smaller (<5 mm).
Late blight lesions are water-soaked without concentric rings and produce white cottony downy mildew on leaf undersides.

potato__early_blight.cultural_management: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers; follow 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops; destroy infected haulms; avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
potato__early_blight.biological_management: Seed tuber dip or foliar spray with Trichoderma viride 1% WP (5 g/L) or Bacillus subtilis; spray neem oil 1500 ppm (4 ml/L) at first symptom appearance.
potato__early_blight.chemical_management: Preventive spray of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0-2.5 g/L water (600 g/acre). At moderate severity, spray Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L water (200 ml/acre). PHI: 7 days.
potato__early_blight.preventive_measures: Seed tuber treatment with Trichoderma viride (5 g/kg); maintain balanced potassium fertilization (reduces plant susceptibility); hill up soil properly.
potato__early_blight.authoritative_references: ICAR-CPRI Technical Bulletin No. 94; SDAU Sardarkrushinagar Potato Pathology Compendium

potato__late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly enlarging water-soaked irregular lesions turning purplish-brown/black, delicate white cottony downy fungal sporulation on lower leaf margins under high humidity; necrotic stem lesions; copper-brown dry granular rot on tuber periderm.
potato__late_blight.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Hemibiotrophic oomycete reproducing via biflagellate motile zoospores released from lemon-shaped sporangia. Causes explosive epidemics in cold, foggy weather.
potato__late_blight.favourable_environmental_conditions: Cool temperatures (10-20°C) with persistent high relative humidity (>90%) for >12 hours; dense fog spells in north Gujarat (Banaskantha) during December-January.
potato__late_blight.transmission_mechanism: Wind-borne sporangia travelling over kilometers; infected latent seed tubers; water-splashing.
potato__late_blight.diagnostic_characteristics: Rapidly enlarging water-soaked purplish-brown/black lesions on leaf margins with delicate white downy cottony sporulation visible on abaxial surface during humid mornings; dark greasy stem lesions.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Early blight has concentric dry target rings without white downy sporulation.
Blackleg causes jet-black slimy stem decay originating at ground line, not foliar downy blighting.

potato__late_blight.cultural_management: Install early warning blite-cast alert; rogue out volunteer potato plants and cull piles; plant resistant varieties (e.g. Kufri Badshah, Kufri Pukhraj); dehaulm 10 days before harvest.
potato__late_blight.biological_management: Prophylactic application of bio-agents (Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L) before weather conditions become conducive for blight.
potato__late_blight.chemical_management: Prophylactic spray: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water. Upon first blight alert: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5-3.0 g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L + Mancozeb (2.0 g/L). PHI: 7-10 days.
potato__late_blight.preventive_measures: Pre-sowing seed tuber dip in Mancozeb (2.5 g/L); avoid irrigation during cold cloudy days; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer that produces dense succulent canopies.
potato__late_blight.authoritative_references: ICAR-CPRI Disease Management Bulletin; PPQ&S Integrated Pest Management Package for Potato

potato__black_scurf.symptoms: Hard, superficial, irregular brownish-black sclerotial encrustations resembling dirt particles ('dirt that won't wash off') adhering tightly to tuber skin; brown sunken lesions/cankers on subterranean sprouts and stolons.
potato__black_scurf.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Basidiomycete fungus forming resting sclerotia that adhere to tuber surfaces; subterranean hyphae attack emerging stolons.
potato__black_scurf.favourable_environmental_conditions: Cold, damp soil at planting time; prolonged exposure of tubers in wet soil before harvesting.
potato__black_scurf.transmission_mechanism: Seed-borne tuber sclerotia and soil-borne mycelium surviving in soil organic matter.
potato__black_scurf.diagnostic_characteristics: Hard, superficial, irregular brownish-black sclerotial encrustations adhering tightly to tuber skin ('dirt that won't wash off'); brown sunken cankers on underground sprouts.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Common scab forms corky craters in tuber skin; black scurf deposits are raised, hard resting bodies on intact skin.

potato__black_scurf.cultural_management: Plant tubers shallow in warm soil to encourage fast emergence; shallow harvesting immediately after periderm maturity; practice 3-year crop rotation with maize or sorghum.
potato__black_scurf.biological_management: Seed tuber dip in Trichoderma viride 1% WP slurry @ 5 g/kg seed tuber; apply Trichoderma enriched FYM (2.5 kg/acre) to planting furrows.
potato__black_scurf.chemical_management: Seed tuber dressing before cold storage or planting with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS @ 2.5 g/kg tuber or Pencycuron 250 SC @ 1.5 ml/L water.
potato__black_scurf.preventive_measures: Use certified sclerotia-free seed tubers; ensure proper skin setting before digging; avoid un-decomposed crop residue.
potato__black_scurf.authoritative_references: ICAR-CPRI Annual Report (Rhizoctonia in Banaskantha Sandy-Loam Soils); SDAU Dept of Plant Pathology

potato__common_scab.symptoms: Superficial, raised corky or deeply pitted rough brown stellate lesions with ragged margins on potato tuber skin; leaves and aboveground foliage remain asymptomatic.
potato__common_scab.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Filamentous actinomycete bacterium producing thaxtomin phytotoxins. Survives indefinitely in alkaline, sandy-loam soils.
potato__common_scab.favourable_environmental_conditions: Dry, warm soil conditions during tuber initiation (20-25°C); alkaline soil pH (>6.8); common in light sandy soils of Banaskantha and Mehsana.
potato__common_scab.transmission_mechanism: Infected seed tubers; infested soil; wind-blown dust and irrigation water.
potato__common_scab.diagnostic_characteristics: Rough, raised corky or deeply pitted stellate brown lesions on potato tuber skin; foliage remains completely normal.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Powdery scab pustules rupture to release powdery brown spore balls and have frayed periderm margins.
Black scurf exhibits superficial black sclerotia ('dirt that will not wash off') without corky pitting.

potato__common_scab.cultural_management: Maintain adequate soil moisture during tuber initiation (4-6 weeks after planting); apply green manure (Sesbania/sunnhemp) to lower soil pH; use certified clean seed.
potato__common_scab.biological_management: Seed tuber treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP (10 g/kg) and soil enrichment with Trichoderma viride in FYM.
potato__common_scab.chemical_management: Seed tuber treatment before planting with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L water. Note: Foliar agrochemicals are completely ineffective against tuber scab.
potato__common_scab.preventive_measures: Do not apply fresh uncomposted cattle manure or lime; maintain regular drip irrigation during tuberization to keep soil moisture above 70% available capacity.
potato__common_scab.authoritative_references: ICAR-CPRI Technical Advisory; AAU Anand Soil Microbiology Bulletins

watermelon__anthracnose.symptoms: Circular to irregular dark brown to black spots on leaves, rapidly enlarging and merging, causing blighted 'shot-hole' appearance; elongated sunken dark brown stem lesions; sunken circular circular fruit pits oozing salmon-pink gelatinous spore masses under wet weather.
watermelon__anthracnose.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Fungal pathogen producing hyaline conidia in acervuli with dark setae. Pathogen overwinters in crop refuse and cucurbit seed.
watermelon__anthracnose.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm (24-28°C), wet, rainy weather with frequent precipitation and relative humidity >85%.
watermelon__anthracnose.transmission_mechanism: Rain splash, overhead irrigation, field workers moving through wet foliage, contaminated seed.
watermelon__anthracnose.diagnostic_characteristics: Circular to irregular water-soaked spots on leaves turning dark brown to black, drying and shattering to create a shot-hole look; sunken circular fruit depressions oozing pink gelatinous spore masses under wet weather.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Gummy stem blight produces amber gummy exudate on stems with pycnidia, not pink gelatinous fruit spore masses.
Bacterial fruit blotch produces dark olive-green greasy flat rind blotches without sunken pink spore craters.

watermelon__anthracnose.cultural_management: Use certified pathogen-free seeds; 2-year rotation out of cucurbits; clean up infected vines; avoid field operations when vines are wet.
watermelon__anthracnose.biological_management: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 1% WP (10 g/kg seed); foliar bio-fungicide sprays at early vine development.
watermelon__anthracnose.chemical_management: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0-2.5 g/L water as protective cover. Curative: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L water. PHI: 7 days.
watermelon__anthracnose.preventive_measures: Pre-sowing seed soak in Thiram or Captan (2 g/kg); sub-surface drip irrigation to avoid leaf splashing.
watermelon__anthracnose.authoritative_references: AAU Anand Plant Pathology Bulletin; ICAR-CIAH Cucurbitaceous Crop Manual

watermelon__downy_mildew.symptoms: Bright yellow, chlorotic, angular lesions sharply delimited by leaf veins on upper leaf surface ('checkerboard pattern'); purplish-gray to blackish downy felt-like sporulation on corresponding lower leaf surface during high humidity; leaves curl inward, scorch brown, and die.
watermelon__downy_mildew.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Obligate biotrophic oomycete with branched sporangiophores bearing oval sporangia. Infects through open stomata on the lower leaf surface.
watermelon__downy_mildew.favourable_environmental_conditions: High relative humidity (>85%), morning dew, temperatures between 16-24°C; frequent spring morning fogs in Anand/Kheda cucurbit tracts.
watermelon__downy_mildew.transmission_mechanism: Wind-blown sporangia transported across long distances; splashing rain/overhead irrigation.
watermelon__downy_mildew.diagnostic_characteristics: Bright yellow, chlorotic, angular lesions sharply delimited by leaf veins on upper leaf surface ('checkerboard' appearance); purplish-gray to dark downy sporulation on the underside.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Angular leaf spot lesions are water-soaked, tear away into shot-holes, and lack purplish-gray downy sporulation.
Powdery mildew produces white talcum-like circular powdery colonies on upper leaf surfaces, not yellow angular blocks.

watermelon__downy_mildew.cultural_management: Adopt drip irrigation; avoid overhead watering; provide wider vine spacing (2.5 - 3.0 m) for canopy aeration; rogue out early infected leaves.
watermelon__downy_mildew.biological_management: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L water; prophylactic sprays of copper hydroxide (2 g/L) before epidemic build-up.
watermelon__downy_mildew.chemical_management: Preventive: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0-2.5 g/L. At first angular lesion: Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1.0-1.25 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L water (600 g/acre). PHI: 7-10 days.
watermelon__downy_mildew.preventive_measures: Early morning irrigation; utilize mulch to avoid fruit-soil contact; plant resistant/tolerant hybrids.
watermelon__downy_mildew.authoritative_references: AAU Anand Research Bulletin; JAU Junagadh Agricultural University Crop Protection Handbook

watermelon__powdery_mildew.symptoms: Distinctive white, powdery, talcum-like circular fungal spots starting on lower older leaves, expanding over upper and lower leaf surfaces, petioles, and young stems; infected foliage turns chlorotic, dull brown, brittle, and withers prematurely; exposed fruit sunscalds.
watermelon__powdery_mildew.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Ectophytic fungal parasite producing barrel-shaped conidia in chains on superficial hyphae. Haustoria penetrate epidermal cells.
watermelon__powdery_mildew.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm (22-30°C), dry weather with shaded foliage; low sunlight; prevalent in late spring / summer watermelon crops in Gujarat.
watermelon__powdery_mildew.transmission_mechanism: Air-borne conidia carried by wind currents; does not require free water on leaves for germination.
watermelon__powdery_mildew.diagnostic_characteristics: Distinctive white, powdery, talcum-like circular spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces and petioles; leaves become chlorotic, brittle, curl upward, and scorch.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Downy mildew causes angular yellow blocks with gray-purple undersides, not white talcum powder.
Chemical residue wipes off without cellular chlorosis and shows uniform droplet contours.

watermelon__powdery_mildew.cultural_management: Maintain good plant vigor; eradicate wild cucurbit weeds; prune dense foliage to allow sunlight penetration.
watermelon__powdery_mildew.biological_management: Spray Ampelomyces quisqualis (hyperparasite) or Bacillus subtilis @ 5 g/L; neem oil 1500 ppm @ 4 ml/L water.

watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.scientific_name: Acidovorax citrulli (syn. Acidovorax avenae subsp. citrulli)
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.symptoms: Small water-soaked greasy olive-green streaks on seedling cotyledons; on maturing fruit, large dark olive-green water-soaked greasy blotches (10 to 30 cm) with irregular margins appearing on upper fruit surface; rind cracks with amber bacterial exudate.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Seed-borne Gram-negative rod bacterium that invades through stomata on young developing fruit rinds.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.favourable_environmental_conditions: High temperatures (28-35°C) combined with high relative humidity, rainstorms, and overhead irrigation.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.transmission_mechanism: Primary transmission via infected commercial seed; secondary spread via wind-driven rain, irrigation splashing, and pruning tools.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.diagnostic_characteristics: Small water-soaked greasy olive-green streaks on seedling leaves; on mature melons, large dark olive-green water-soaked greasy blotches (10 to 30 cm) with irregular boundaries appearing on upper fruit rind; rind fissures with amber exudate.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Sunscald produces dry, bleached, papery white lesions on upper rind, not greasy dark-green water-soaked blotches.
Anthracnose causes sunken circular pitted craters with pink spore masses.

watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.cultural_management: Use rigorously certified tested disease-free hybrid seed; sanitize seedling trays with 10% sodium hypochlorite; destroy infected seedlings immediately; avoid overhead irrigation.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.biological_management: Seed bacterization with Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP (10 g/kg seed) to competitively exclude Acidovorax colonization.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.chemical_management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5-3.0 g/L water (600 g/acre) combined with Streptocycline (bactericide) @ 1.0 g per 10 L water (100 ppm). PHI: 5 days.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.preventive_measures: Quarantine inspections; hot-water seed treatment (50°C for 20 min); strictly avoid entering watermelon fields during wet morning hours.
watermelon__bacterial_fruit_blotch.authoritative_references: EPPO Quarantine Data Sheet; Directorate of PPQ&S Seed Health Testing Guidelines

watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Chrysomelid beetle; bright orange-red adults feed on foliage and cotyledons; subterranean creamy grubs feed on taproots and underground stems.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm spring and summer months (February to May); peak activity in cotyledon and early vegetative seedling stages.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.transmission_mechanism: Active adult flight from overwintering soil sites; subterranean larval crawling in root rhizosphere.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.diagnostic_characteristics: Bright orange-red oblong beetles (6-8 mm) chewing circular and semi-circular feeding holes/notches in cotyledons and leaves; skeletonized seedling foliage.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Cutworms sever the entire seedling vine at soil surface overnight; pumpkin beetles cut circular feeding holes in leaf laminae during daytime.

watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.cultural_management: Early morning manual collection of sluggish beetles using hand nets; clean cultivation; deep summer ploughing to expose subterranean pupae and grubs to solar heat and predatory birds.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.biological_management: Apply Neem cake to soil @ 100 kg/acre; spray Azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 4 ml/L water as antifeedant; dust wood ash on cotyledons during early dawn.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.chemical_management: At economic threshold (1 beetle/plant on seedlings): Spray Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3 ml/L water (60 ml/acre) or Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD @ 1.8 ml/L water. PHI: 3-5 days.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.preventive_measures: Protect early seedlings using insect net covers or row covers during the first 2-3 weeks until 4-leaf stage; dust fine ash mixed with neem powder on seedlings.
watermelon__red_pumpkin_beetle.authoritative_references: AAU Anand Agricultural Entomology Bulletin; SDAU Banaskantha Pest Calendar

watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.symptoms: Female fruit fly punctures tender developing fruit skin to lay eggs; tiny puncture spots ooze translucent amber resinous fluid; fruit develops sunken deformity, rot, premature yellowing, and interior liquefaction packed with white jumping maggots.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Tephritid dipteran fly with prominent yellow longitudinal dorsal stripe on thorax and banded wings. Female oviposits beneath young fruit rind.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm, humid conditions; fruiting stage through harvest; high temperatures (26-32°C).
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.transmission_mechanism: Strong-flying adult flies traveling across fields; transport of infested rotting melons.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.diagnostic_characteristics: Punctures on young tender melons with oozing brown resinous droplet weeping from skin; fruit develops sunken curvature/deformity, internal liquefaction packed with white jumping maggots.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Blossom end rot is a dry, flat leathery patch at distal blossom tip without puncture droplets or internal maggots.

watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.cultural_management: Promptly collect and bury all punctured, deformed, or dropped melons in deep pits (>60 cm) with lime; bag developing fruits with paper bags on small acreage; deep post-harvest soil tilling.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.biological_management: Install Cue-lure pheromone traps (Male Annihilation Technique) @ 6-8 traps per acre at canopy height; replace lures every 30-40 days.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.chemical_management: Bait Spray: Mix Malathion 50% EC @ 2.0 ml + Jaggery/Molasses (100 g) per 10 L water; apply coarse droplets to underside of border vegetation (not direct fruit spray). PHI: 5 days.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.preventive_measures: Field sanitation; install fruit fly traps before blossom initiation; maintain border trap crops.
watermelon__melon_fruit_fly.authoritative_references: ICAR-CIAH Bikaner IPM Guidelines; AAU Anand Entomology Advisory

watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.symptoms: Conspicuous, slender, white to translucent serpentine winding mines and wandering tunnels meandering irregularly across leaf lamina; black frass trail visible within mine; heavy mining causes complete foliar drying.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Agromyzid dipteran fly. Female punctures leaf to oviposit; yellow legless larva mines within mesophyll tissue between epidermal layers.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm, sunny, dry weather (25-32°C); continuous cucurbit, tomato, and cotton cropping.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.transmission_mechanism: Adult fly dispersal; nursery transport of infested seedlings.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.diagnostic_characteristics: Conspicuous white to translucent winding serpentine tunnels meandering irregularly across leaf lamina with black frass grains inside.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: PTM produces irregular blotch mines, not narrow winding serpentine ribbons.

watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.cultural_management: Hand-pick and crush mined cotyledons and early leaves; install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre); destroy solanaceous and cucurbit weed hosts.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.biological_management: Conserve native eulophid parasitoids (Diglyphus isaea); spray Azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 4 ml/L water to disrupt larval development and deter adult oviposition.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.chemical_management: At economic threshold (2-3 active mines per leaf): Spray Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD @ 1.8-2.0 ml/L water (translaminar larvicide) or Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.35 ml/L water. PHI: 5 days.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.preventive_measures: Do not spray broad-spectrum pyrethroids which wipe out natural leafminer parasitoid wasps; install yellow sticky traps before seedling emergence.
watermelon__leaf_miner_serpentine_leafmi.authoritative_references: AAU Anand Entomology Bulletin; ICAR-IIVR Insect Pest Compendium

watermelon__blossom_end_rot.symptoms: Small water-soaked lesion at blossom end (distal tip) of developing fruit, enlarging into a large, flat, sunken, leathery, dark brown to black dry necrotic patch; secondary fungi may colonize necrotic spot.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Abiotic physiological disorder caused by localized calcium deficiency in rapidly expanding distal fruit tissues, exacerbated by erratic irrigation and water stress.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.favourable_environmental_conditions: Rapid fruit expansion during hot, dry, windy days; fluctuating soil moisture (drought followed by heavy irrigation); high nitrogen fertilization.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.transmission_mechanism: Non-infectious abiotic disorder. Zero pathogen transmission.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.diagnostic_characteristics: Sunken, flat, dry, leathery, dark brown to black circular patch at the distal blossom end of the melon fruit.

similar_looking_conditions.distinction: Anthracnose fruit rot produces sunken circular pits with pink spore slime scattered all over the rind, not exclusively at the blossom tip.
Fruit fly exhibits resinous puncture weep points and maggot liquefaction.

watermelon__blossom_end_rot.cultural_management: Maintain consistent, uniform soil moisture using drip irrigation; apply plastic or straw mulch to stabilize root-zone moisture; avoid cultivating too close to vine roots.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.biological_management: Soil application of organic compost and mycorrhizal fungi to enhance root surface area and calcium uptake.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.chemical_management: Agrochemicals/pesticides are strictly prohibited! Apply foliar spray of Chelated Calcium (Ca-EDTA) @ 1.5 g/L or Calcium Nitrate @ 3.0-5.0 g/L water during early fruit set. Repeat at 10-day intervals.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.preventive_measures: Conduct pre-season soil test; avoid excessive ammonium-based nitrogen (NH4+ competes with Ca2+ uptake); ensure steady irrigation scheduling throughout fruit bulking.
watermelon__blossom_end_rot.authoritative_references: AAU Anand Horticulture Extension Bulletins; ICAR-IIVR Varanasi Advisory

watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.symptoms: Vigorous, sprawling vines with deep-green deeply lobed foliage, clean yellow flowers, vibrant unblemished tendrils, healthy developing melons with uniform rind patterns and no lesion or pest damage.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.disease_causes_or_pest_biology: Vigorous, healthy Citrullus lanatus vine with balanced vegetative and reproductive development.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.favourable_environmental_conditions: Warm sunny days (24-32°C), well-drained sandy loam soil with pH 6.0-7.0, regular drip fertigation.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.diagnostic_characteristics: Deep green crisp lobed leaves, vibrant yellow flowers, sturdy tendrils, uniform unblemished melon rinds, absence of spots, chlorosis, or webbing.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.cultural_management: Maintain scheduled drip fertigation, honeybee pollination conservation, weed sanitation, and uniform soil moisture.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.biological_management: Erect yellow sticky traps for prophylactic insect monitoring; conserve beneficial predatory insects.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.chemical_management: Agrochemical application is strictly prohibited on healthy plants! Maintain standard agronomic fertigation.
watermelon__healthy_watermelon_plant.preventive_measures: Routine scouting every 3-4 days to detect earliest signs of downy mildew or sucking pests.
